ashby:1mind:74f0b798-c99b-421e-866f-8c61.summary: This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

sections.title: 1mind is building the next generation of revenue teams.
paras: We are creating a new category of enterprise software: Autonomous Customer Experience. Our platform deploys Superhumans , go-to-market teammates with a face, a voice, and a GTM brain that serve the buyer across the entire journey with one continuous memory. They engage, demo, onboard, and support in the moments no company could ever staff, so the handoffs disappear and growth stops leaking.
Join us as we define the category and build the platform that powers the next generation of revenue teams. When the buyer wins, the company wins. Every1 Wins.

sections.title: About the role
paras: 1mind is building the AI-led GTM workforce: Superhumans that run SDR, SE, onboarding, AM and CSM work end to end, on top of a shared context graph that compounds across every customer conversation. Superhumans win or lose in the moments a buyer meets one: the live conversation, the demo, the follow-up. The Superhuman Console is where customers create them: persona, goals, knowledge, guardrails, testing and analytics. Today both still lean on our team. The next product leap is self-serve craft: a Superhuman a buyer prefers over a human rep, built and tuned by the customer in an afternoon rather than by us over weeks.

You own that leap. This is the PM seat for the app layer, covering the Superhuman experience and the Superhuman Console, working with our Head of Product, our conversational AI design team and the app engineering teams, and reporting to the Chief Product Officer. You decide what a buyer sees, hears and clicks in every conversation with a Superhuman, and what a customer touches to build, tune and measure one. The Agents & Orchestration PM owns the runtime underneath; you own everything customers and buyers see on top of it.

The bar is unforgiving. Buyers do not grade AI on a curve: a Superhuman either beats the best rep they have met or gets dismissed in the first minute. Expect to ship weekly and raise the craft bar while you do.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Superhuman experience. The live conversation surface across web, voice and video: pre-call prep, in-call assists, interactive demos and screen share, post-call follow-through. Latency, interruption handling, and the hundred small choices that decide whether a buyer stays in the conversation or closes the tab.

Superhuman Console. The builder: persona, goals, ICP, knowledge, guardrails, preview and test, publish. You own how fast a customer gets from blank page to a live Superhuman, and how much of the tuning they can do without anyone from 1mind in the room.

Self-serve and activation. Signup to first live conversation with no human from 1mind in the loop: onboarding, first-time user experience, templates, and defaults that work out of the box. Time to first value is your headline metric.

Analytics and value reporting. The dashboards customers run the product from: pipeline influenced, meetings advanced, deals touched, not just conversation counts. You build the chart a champion forwards to their VP at renewal time.

Personalization. Workspace-level configuration today, per-rep personalization next, with reps holding the controls. Shared context from the graph surfacing at the right moment on every surface, so each Superhuman gets smarter with every conversation the customer has.

Release process. Weekly ship cadence with design and engineering, enablement and CS looped in before each release, and the design quality bar for every customer-facing surface, held jointly with our conversational AI designer.

sections.title: What You’ll Bring
bullets: 5+ years of product management, with at least 2 years on an AI-native product where the user-facing experience was the product, not a feature bolted onto SaaS.

Craft obsession. You have owned a surface users loved, at an AI-native company or a craft-first product company, ideally paired with founder or early-startup experience. You sweat latency, motion, empty states and copy. We are not looking for feature-factory PMs.
You have built or owned a builder, editor or configuration product and know the line between flexible and confusing. You can explain why a default beats a setting.
You think in funnels: signup to activation to habit. You have moved time-to-first-value and retention numbers you can quote, and you instrument before you ship.

Technical enough to work with the runtime team: you know what prompt, context and config changes can fix versus what needs the model team, and you can read a conversation trace and tell us where the experience broke.
You prototype with code or design tools before you write a doc, and you would rather fix a v1 in production than polish a v2 in Figma.
Clear writing. Your specs are short, your dashboards have the numbers that matter, and your Slack messages make sense to sales.

ashby:benchling:3b50ebb7-4e9e-4ede-aaf7-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: Benchling's platform helps the world's largest biotech and pharma companies develop therapies faster. As a Product Manager on the Scientific Development Solutions team, you'll work on products such as Recipes, Assays, and Workflows that scientists use to do their jobs. These products are fundamental to how scientific processes get configured, run, and tracked across different phases of a drug's development cycle.

We launched Bioprocess in 2024 to help process development teams design, execute, and analyze the experiments that turn a molecule into a manufacturable drug. In 2025, we announced a partnership with Merck ( press release ) to help their teams develop and test vaccines faster by bringing their analytical workflows onto a single platform.

Today, we're implementing the largest pharma companies in the world on Bioprocess, making the core product better every quarter, and expanding into Analytical Sciences and downstream QC. Our vision is to become the software that helps biopharmas bring therapies to patients twice as fast.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: You are responsible for Recipes, Assays, and Workflows. That means you and your team decide what gets built, why, and in what order. You're accountable for the roadmap and the outcomes your roadmap produces.

To inform what you build, you will spend time with customers and GTM teams to understand how scientists actually work, and how to turn what they ask for into what they need. It's your responsibility to bring that context back to the team and turn it into product direction.

You'll work alongside design, engineering, GTM, and our customers to build and ship products. That means guiding product decisions with design and engineering, validating ideas early with customers, enabling customer experience teams on what you ship, and partnering with GTM to bring it to market.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: 3-5+ years of product management or equivalent experience

A diverse career history. You've worked across 2-3+ meaningfully different domains or product types. This is the single strongest signal we're looking for. It tells us you're a systems thinker who adapts, not someone who relies on one playbook.

Technical tool competency. You're resourceful. You use tools to help yourself and your team get work done, whether that's writing SQL queries to make data-driven decisions, using design tools to create prototypes, or using something like Cursor to ship product improvements directly.

Clear communication. You can lead an engaging professional conversation and keep a room's attention. You know how to adapt your communication style based on your audience and can read and respond to the individuals in the conversation. As a PM, this matters almost more than anything else.
Track record of outcomes. You've stayed long enough at key roles to ship, learn, and speak to what worked and what didn't. We're looking for evidence of impact.

Intellectual range. You're genuinely curious, and that curiosity shows up in how you learn and think about problems. Product management is a means to an end. It's how you apply the learnings from the curiosity that has driven you. What you and your team decide to build is an inevitable conclusion of that curiosity.

bullets: Experience in regulated or compliance-heavy industries (doesn't have to be life sciences)
Configuration-heavy, platform-style products
B2B SaaS in the growth/scaling stage
Prior life as an engineer, data scientist, or solutions consultant

ashby:crusoe:c08a297f-2be4-467f-85c0-24f.summary:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: As the Principal Product Manager, Bare Metal, you'll own the strategy and outcomes for a brand-new initiative at Crusoe: our bare metal offering, giving AI-native companies direct GPU and CPU access to power the world's most demanding training and inference workloads. This is a role at the intersection of hardware and software, spanning compute, networking, observability, and management. You will be defining the problem space as much as solving it. You should be genuinely comfortable operating in ambiguity, though you won't be doing it alone: you'll have support from senior leadership to help clean up open questions as the initiative takes shape.

This role blends Product Management, Solutions Architecture and Process Design. You will need technical depth spanning across the hardware, firmware and operating system layers (e.g. BMC — Baseboard Management Controller, secure boot) as well as the process rigor to design how the product behaves operationally.

sections.title: What You'll Be Working On:
bullets: Roadmap Ownership: Drive the vision for bare metal compute, encompassing GPU/CPU offerings, rapid provisioning systems, and full lifecycle management.

Process & Operational Design: Define the end-to-end customer experience when something goes wrong — the ticketing workflow, escalation paths, and process behind it — in close partnership with Infrastructure Operations and Customer Support.
Outcome Management: Ensure tight alignment between hardware and software layers to deliver a differentiated bare metal experience.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead initiatives across engineering and infra-ops to deliver provisioning, enhanced observability, and customer self-service capabilities.
Customer & Market Synthesis: Partner with Sales and GTM teams to transform customer feedback into roadmap priorities, ensuring deep product-market fit.

Executive Representation: Represent the bare metal strategy to partners and internal executives, framing technical infrastructure decisions within a clear business context and treating this portfolio like a business you're accountable for.

sections.title: What You'll Bring to the Team:
bullets: Infrastructure Leadership: 10+ years of experience in cloud and computing technology, including 4+ years in product management focused on infrastructure or platform products, with a track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives through ambiguity.
Hardware Depth: Direct experience at the hardware and firmware level, you don't need to be an engineer, but you need to have worked at that layer.
Process Orientation: A demonstrated ability to design and formalize operational processes (support workflows, ticketing, incident handling) for a technical product
Deep Compute & Operational Expertise: Comprehensive knowledge of server hardware, bare metal provisioning, distributed systems, networking, and large-scale fleet operations.
Strategic Decision Making: Proven ability to navigate ambiguous, ill-defined problem spaces and drive long-term vision while balancing technical constraints and business outcomes
Communication Mastery: The ability to articulate deep technical complexity to executive audiences and translate business goals into clear product direction.

Technical Tooling: Familiarity with IPMI/BMC protocols, infrastructure automation tools, or bare metal provisioning frameworks.
AI/ML Domain Knowledge: An understanding of GPU-based AI workloads and their specific demands on compute and network infrastructure.

ashby:duffel:018b4fe7-9571-46a8-8ff7-26b.summary:

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Data powers nearly every part of Leap: launching new clients, identifying patients, coordinating care, sourcing drugs, and measuring savings. As we grow, more teams depend on our data platform, and their needs often compete for the same engineering capacity.

You’ll own the product direction and delivery of Leap’s data platform and integrations. A central part of your role will be bringing structure to how work reaches Data Engineering: understanding requests across teams, clarifying the underlying needs, and making explicit decisions about what gets prioritized, when, and why. You’ll build a process that makes it easier for teams to get their needs addressed and for engineers to focus on the most important work.

Working closely with our data engineers, you’ll turn those priorities into well-scoped projects with clear milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Your remit will span our ingestion engine, data quality and traceability, and integrations that embed Leap into client and partner workflows. Engineering owns architecture and implementation; you’ll help define the capabilities we need and sequence investments alongside immediate business commitments.

sections.title: Intake & Cross-Team Prioritization

Work with requesters to understand the problem, business impact, urgency, and downstream dependencies before committing engineering capacity.
Reconcile competing needs across teams, distinguish firm deadlines from preferred timing, and make trade-offs explicit.
Maintain a single prioritized backlog and roadmap that balance client launches, business needs, platform improvements, and reliability.
Resolve conflicting requests with stakeholders and bring decisions that require leadership input forward with clear options and a recommendation.
Keep teams informed about what is committed, what is deferred, and why. Revisit priorities as needs change, with a clear view of the impact on existing commitments.
Continually improve intake so that gathering requirements and reaching decisions require less back-and-forth as Leap grows.

sections.title: Product Ownership & Delivery
bullets: Translate prioritized needs into clear problem statements, requirements, dependencies, and measurable acceptance criteria.
Work with engineers to break projects into deliverable milestones, test assumptions, and establish realistic timelines.
Coordinate dependencies across teams and external partners so work is ready to proceed when engineering capacity is available.
Track delivery, surface risks early, and agree on changes to scope or timing with the teams affected.

Support engineering-led architecture and tooling decisions by clarifying business requirements and weighing implications for delivery, reliability, cost, and future needs.
Define requirements for data provenance: where data comes from, how it is transformed, where it is used, and who is responsible for it.
Establish expectations for freshness, completeness, and accuracy with data consumers, and work with engineering on monitoring, alerting, and escalation.
Ensure sources, data contracts, ownership, and key platform decisions are documented; drive recurring data quality issues toward durable resolution.
Partner with Analytics on metric lineage and with Security on requirements for access controls, PHI handling, retention, and third-party data use.

This role exists to make sure each of them sees Legora as built specifically for them. You'll take the operating-model narrative for how an AI-first legal team works and adapt it into practice- and segment-specific playbooks: positioning, proof points, and materials that translate our platform's depth into concrete reasons to buy. The sharpness of that translation is what determines whether we win the room or get bucketed alongside every other AI vendor in the market.

The ideal candidate has spent the better part of a decade owning solutions or vertical product marketing in high-growth enterprise SaaS or AI environments. They know how to take a single product and shape it into distinct, buyer-specific narratives without fragmenting the brand or diluting the message. They understand how to partner with sales on the deals that matter, how to build the materials that move pipeline, and how to land a launch that holds together across product, sales, and customer-facing teams. ashby:partly.com:ad39610e-39eb-4a02-af41.summary: Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. sections.title: 🚀 Our Story
paras: Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly .

sections.title: 🖍️ This role
paras: As Partly's first Implementation & Customer Success Manager in the US, you'll found the function that makes shops successful after they sign. You'll own implementation, onboarding and retention for independent collision shops and multi-shop operators (MSOs) with up to 20 locations.

You work hand in hand with Sales. Once a shop says yes, you take it from there: getting Partly installed and connected, training the team, and making Partly part of how they write and source every job. Then you keep them there. You'll be in shops in person, sometimes flying out to do it, speaking the language of owners, estimators and parts managers.

You're also our product expert in the field. You'll spend time in shops, understand the problems behind what they ask for, and separate what one shop wants from what most shops need. Sometimes the answer is a feature; often it's a workaround that gets the job done today. You'll bring what matters back to Product with the evidence to act on it. As the first hire, you'll build the playbook, processes and metrics the US customer team grows on.

sections.title: 💻 What will you do
paras: Want to learn more about the problems we're solving and the culture we're building at Partly? Hear directly from our team here: https://shorturl.at/iAFUX
bullets: Own implementation and onboarding. Take the handoff from Sales and run every new shop's implementation end to end. Install Partly, connect it to the shop's estimating system, train the team and get them sourcing parts through Partly in their first week.
Run pilots that convert. Implement shop pilots end to end, track activation against agreed success criteria, and turn pilots into live, retained shops.
Support Sales. Step in before signature when a shop needs a technical walkthrough or proof that it will work in their environment.

Drive activation and retention. Get every shop to daily use and keep them there. Run regular check-ins, lift usage of the features that matter, spot churn risk early and win back shops that have gone quiet.
Be the shop's trusted contact. Be the day-to-day contact for shop owners, estimators and parts managers, and the person they call when something isn't working.
Show up in person. Visit shops on site to implement, troubleshoot and build relationships, including regular travel across the US.

Resolve issues to ground. Diagnose where a shop is stuck, whether that's installation, the estimating integration or their workflow. Fix what you can yourself and work with Engineering on the rest, rather than just passing tickets on.

Bring product thinking to the shop floor. Understand what's really behind a shop's request. Tell the difference between what one shop wants and what most shops need, and back it with what you saw across shops.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

sections.title: ABOUT THE TEAM
paras:
Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build the software-defined shipyard. That means the full technology stack running Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, ArsenalOS (our manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift), the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

This work is anchored by Arsenal-2, our software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of that yard. It connects fabrication and outfitting to material movement and inspection. Planners get one real-time view of production. We aren't waiting for the yard to open. Development is already underway here in Orange County, California. The team is proving out the manufacturing methods and digital workflows that will scale across the shipyard network.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.

Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what…

lever:supermove:5f52760f-d54d-49b3-813c-.summary:
Supermove builds software and AI for moving companies. We've raised $30M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors. We started in 2019 as the system that runs a moving business: sales, operations, crews, billing. Today that system runs moving companies across the US, Canada and Australia, from single-location movers to some of the largest van lines and franchise systems in North America.

Now we're putting AI to work on top of it. Our voice agents answer and call leads, book moves, and hand off to a person at the right moment. Autopilot, our agent platform, goes further. It answers questions about the business in plain language, flags what needs attention, and handles work that used to take a person's whole day, from working the inbox to updating jobs.

sections.title: The role
paras: Every moving company runs on its own logic: its own rates and tariffs, its own way of paying crews and commissioning salespeople, its own accounting system, and often a van line with rules of its own. When a customer signs, someone has to turn all of that into a working Supermove account. That's you.

You'll own implementations from kickoff to go-live and a clean handoff to our customer success team, running several at once. On our largest accounts, you'll work alongside a Key Account Director who owns the relationship and the results. You own the build.

This is a hands-on role. You won't write requirements and hand them to someone else. You'll be inside Supermove every day, configuring, testing, and tracing why an invoice or a sync came out wrong. The people who love this job would rather be in the tool than reporting on it.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Run implementations from kickoff to go-live: discovery, configuration, testing, training, launch. Set the dates and hold the customer and our team to them.
Turn how a customer charges and pays into working configuration: pricing and tariffs, billing formulas, hourly minimums, crew pay, and salesperson and contract-driver commissions.
Design account structures for multi-location companies and franchise systems, and build master templates that dozens or hundreds of locations can start from.
Set up and fix accounting integrations. Map the general ledger, get invoices and vendor bills flowing to Sage Intacct or QuickBooks, and help the customer's finance team reconcile.
Connect customers to their van lines (Unigroup, SIRVA and others) so orders, statements and settlements flow without retyping.
Set up voice agents and Autopilot workflows with the customer. Decide where the AI acts on its own and where a person signs off, then listen to real calls and fix what's failing.

Use AI agents to do the work faster: investigating issues, drafting configuration, working through data, answering customer questions. Then help define what our own configuration and Autopilot agents should do next.
Turn what customers run into into clear bug reports and product requests, with screenshots and the customer's own words, and follow them through with engineering.

sections.title: What this role asks of you
bullets: Comfort with how money moves. You know what a general ledger, AP and AR, a vendor bill and a reconciliation are, and you can talk to a controller in their language.
Logic and formulas. You can turn a commission sheet or a rate contract into rules a system can run, and spot the case that breaks them.

Comfort ahead of the documentation. We're putting AI into an industry that's never had it, so there's often no runbook yet. You'll design the approach while running it, then write it down so the next implementation starts further ahead.
AI as a working tool. You already use AI to get more done, not as a novelty. Candidates who've built it into how they work stand out.
Patience with a low-tech user base. Dispatchers, sales reps, and owners who've run the same way for twenty years. Changing how they work takes credibility on the ground as much as a project plan.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: 5+ years implementing or configuring complex business software (ERP, accounting, payroll, field-service, or vertical SaaS) for customers, owning the go-live. Experience with field-heavy businesses like construction, home services, fleet or logistics is a plus.
Accounting or bookkeeping experience is a big plus.
Technical enough to troubleshoot. You understand APIs, webhooks and data syncs well enough to tell where something broke. SQL or light scripting is a plus.
You've run several projects at once without dropping any, and you can tell us how.
Clear and steady with customers, whether you're training a dispatcher or telling a controller why the numbers don't match yet.
You write clearly. A lot of this job happens in writing.
Moving, van-line or relocation experience is a plus. We'll teach you the industry.

Our solutions are designed to reduce the pressure on care professionals while improving the quality of care. In short: we want to improve the quality of life for LTC residents and make the work of care professionals a little easier every day.

paras: As an Account Manager at Momo, you are the trusted face of Momo for existing and potential LTC organizations in your region.

You build relationships with management teams and care professionals and help LTC organizations explore Momo through a free pilot. For us, success is not about making a quick sale. You are comfortable with change . Momo Canada is still growing and not everything has a playbook yet. You enjoy figuring things out, sharing what you learn and adapting along the way.

smartrecruiters:servicenow:7440001545414.summary:
We are looking for a Director of Product Management to lead a team of PMs as well as own the product strategy for empowering developers on the Now platform to build and take their applications to production faster. These areas include developer reach, testing, sandboxing, metering, and deployment of AI and human generated code.

As agentic build tools compress the time it takes to author a change, the bottleneck moves downstream. Testing and deploying safely to production is already one of the loudest customer asks and one of the sharpest pain points on the platform. When changes originate from agents as well as people, and arrive at a much higher rate, the ability to validate and trust them quickly stops being a quality-of-life improvement and becomes a precondition for platform growth. You will lead the team that enables this for developers.

sections.title: Who We're Looking For:
paras: This is not four adjacent feature areas with a shared manager. Customers experience the SDLC as one motion, and the central product challenge of this role is the connective tissue: a sandbox that behaves like the instance you will deploy to, a test suite that knows what changed, a release path that carries the evidence, and a model for building directly in production that an admin can actually govern. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.

The scope is deeply technical and close to execution. The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.

sections.title: What you get to do in this role:
bullets: Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap across Developer Reach, Developer Sandboxes, Agentic Testing, and Release Ops, and define how they compose into one lifecycle from authored change to governed, audited deployment.

Build, lead, and develop a team of PMs, one per area. Set a clear standard for product craft, coach PMs on strategy and execution, and hold the bar on the seams between them: shared primitives, consistent models, and a single coherent customer narrative.

Set product direction for validating AI-originated change at scale: what it means to trust an agent's output, what evidence a release needs to carry, and how much of the test and review burden can be automated without losing accountability.
Drive the Developer Reach strategy, including the product model for building in production with admin control, guardrails, and reversibility at enterprise scale.
Define the sandbox strategy: provisioning speed, production parity, data handling, and the developer experience of getting a safe place to work in seconds rather than days.
Own the release governance path end to end, including the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, and the gating model that makes those tradeoffs explicit rather than accidental.
Shape the metering and cost-modeling strategy for this area in partnership with Pricing & Packaging and Finance, and understand how it impacts the entire App Engine portfolio.
Build the triage discipline that keeps escalations across a broad product surface from displacing the roadmap.

sections.title: To be successful in this role you have:
bullets: Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.

12+ years of product management experience, including experience leading and growing a team of PMs, with a track record of setting technical strategy independently rather than executing a roadmap someone else defined.
A track record of developing PMs, raising the bar on product thinking and execution across a team, and growing earlier-career PMs into strong owners of their areas.
Deep experience owning developer platform, DevOps, or SDLC products at enterprise scale: CI/CD, test automation, environment management, release orchestration, or change management.

Genuine hands-on technical comfort, including reading code, reasoning about system architecture, and holding your own in design discussions with senior engineers. Direct, regular personal use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf in your own workflow.

Experience with enterprise change-management or release-governance systems and the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, ideally including systems that gate deployment through a controlled artifact such as a change set.
Ideally, experience with test strategy at scale: automated test generation, coverage and flakiness economics, regression management, and what it takes for a team to actually trust a green build.
Familiarity with environment and infrastructure provisioning models, ephemeral environments, production parity, and data seeding or masking, and the cost and security tradeoffs each carries.
